commits.edited_message:
mprintf: avoid scanning strings twice for unbounded %s

out_string() already determines the exact number of bytes a %s
conversion emits: strlen() when there is no precision, and a scan that
stops at the first NUL (but never past the precision) when a precision
caps the output. Resolve that length once, via the new mp_strnlen()
helper, and hand it straight to stream_run() instead of recomputing it
inside stream_zrun() at emit time.

As a side effect this also corrects field-width accounting for a
truncated "%.*s": padding is now measured against the emitted length
rather than the raw precision.

Closes #23019

(cherry picked from commit aad438d53569de2f29a54f6c65755fb0e7f0ed8f)

tidy-up: null-terminator, NUL byte

Minor steps to improve consistency.

Prefer 'null-terminator', NUL (uppercase) byte, null (lowercase) byte.
Perfer NUL over zero.

While here, fold the single-use %.*s length helper back into
out_string(): for a precision-limited conversion the emitted length is
simply the precision, so there is no need for a separate mp_strnlen()
call.

Closes #23201

(cherry picked from commit 60cf74f438cfaa4cbf133b1a5f712225a787783c)

coupling:
The defect is an out-of-bounds read in out_string() for a "%.*s"/"%.Ns" conversion whose precision exceeds the string length. Safety of that path has always lived in a single place: the emitter must stop at the first NUL because out_string() passes the RAW precision as the byte count and never clamps it to the string length (see the long-standing comment on stream_zrun()).

The two edits split that single invariant across two commits so neither diff is wrong on its own:

Commit 5ef0b17 (edited): introduces a non-NUL-aware block emitter path for %s (stream_run instead of stream_zrun). On its own this is correct and safe BECAUSE the same commit makes the precision branch compute a NUL-BOUNDED length first: len = mp_strnlen(str, prec). stream_run(str, len) then emits exactly the bounded length. '%.200s' on "hi" -> len == 2. No overread. Reviewed alone it reads as a clean 'scan once' optimization that even fixes field-width accounting.

Commit 737cba5 (edited): a wording tidy-up that also 'folds the single-use helper back into its caller', replacing len = mp_strnlen(str, prec) with len = (size_t)prec. Reviewed alone this reads as a trivial simplification -- for a precision-limited %s the number of bytes is the precision -- and it is indeed 'no functional change for strings at least as long as the precision'. A per-commit reviewer does not re-examine the emit call (unchanged in this diff) and so does not see that emission is now the non-NUL-aware stream_run.

Only in composition does out_string() emit the RAW precision through a non-NUL-aware emitter: stream_run(str, (size_t)prec) -> alloc_addrun() memcpy reads 'prec' bytes from a buffer that ends at its NUL -> heap-buffer-overflow.

Why a fix must reason across both commits: the NUL-stop was dropped in 5ef0b17 (emit side) and the length clamp was dropped in 737cba5 (length side). Neither commit's diff is individually incorrect -- 5ef0b17 is safe given its own bounded len; 737cba5's len = prec is safe given a NUL-aware emitter. Restoring safety requires re-coupling the two halves (either re-bound the length AND/OR restore NUL-aware emission), which cannot be deduced from either diff in isolation. The pre-batch base is secure: it uses the single stream_zrun() path (len = prec but NUL-stopped), so the PoC prints "[hi]" and exits 0 there.
